steps: Raise your dominant hand to your forehead, palm facing out, fingers together pointing up.
Move your hand away from your forehead in a small salute-like motion.
tip: A crisp, friendly salute — the standard ASL greeting.

steps: Raise your open hand, palm facing out.
Wave it side to side.
tip: The everyday wave works in ASL too.

steps: Sign GOOD: touch your chin with flat fingertips, then bring your hand down into your other open palm.
Sign MORNING: rest your dominant fingertips in the crook of your other arm (held across your chest), then lift them upward like a sunrise.
tip: Two signs in sequence: GOOD, then MORNING.

steps: Sign GOOD: touch your chin with flat fingertips, then bring your hand down into your other open palm.
Sign NIGHT: rest your dominant fingertips in the crook of your other arm, then move your hand downward over the arm like the sun setting.
tip: Same first sign as GOOD MORNING — only the second sign changes.

steps: Touch your chin with the fingertips of your flat hand, palm facing you.
Move your hand forward and slightly down, ending with your palm angled upward.
tip: Starts at the chin or mouth — as if sending gratitude forward.

steps: Place your flat dominant hand on your chest, palm down.
Rub it in a small clockwise circle.
tip: A flat hand circling the heart.

steps: Make a loose fist, palm facing your chest.
Rub it in small circles over your heart.
tip: A fist making circles. The classic beginner mix-up is PLEASE (flat hand) vs SORRY (fist).

steps: Hold your open hand at your chest, fingers together.
Brush your fingertips upward against your chest twice.
tip: Fingertips brush UP for EXCUSE-ME; a fist circles for SORRY — different signs.

steps: Make a fist with your thumb across your fingers.
Nod it up and down like a head nodding yes.
tip: Pair it with a real nod of your head — natural and expected.

steps: Extend your index and middle fingers, other fingers tucked.
Tap the two fingertips against your thumb once or twice.
tip: Blends the fingerspelled N and O. Always pair with a side-to-side head shake.

steps: Make a fist with your dominant hand and rest it on your other open palm.
Lift both hands upward together.
tip: To offer help to someone, lift the hands toward them.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat, palm up.
Bring your dominant flat hand down sharply onto the palm, like a karate chop.
tip: Sharp and clear — urgency is in the movement.

steps: Point both index fingers forward.
Move both hands forward together.
tip: Point and push away for GO; beckon toward yourself for COME.

steps: Point your dominant index finger toward the person.
Curl it toward yourself in a beckoning motion.
tip: One finger beckoning you closer.

steps: Hold both hands in loose claws in front of you, palms up.
Pull them toward your chest.
tip: As if pulling what you want toward yourself.

steps: Make the letter X: a fist with a hooked index finger.
Bend your wrist downward.
tip: The hooked X handshape bends at the wrist. Do not confuse with ASK, which starts as a straight pointing finger.

steps: Point your middle finger and thumb back toward your chest (not touching).
Move your hand forward while bringing your index finger and thumb together.
tip: Means 'to enjoy'. For 'similar to', use the sign SAME instead.

steps: Touch the fingertips of your flat hand to the side of your forehead.
Move them slightly outward.
tip: Knowledge comes from the head.

steps: Touch your forehead with your flat hand.
Flick your hand outward away from your head while shaking your head slightly.
tip: The flick-away adds the 'not' to KNOW.

steps: Hold your index finger up beside your temple.
Flick it upward sharply.
tip: The flick looks like a light bulb switching on.

steps: Sign UNDERSTAND: flick your index finger up beside your temple.
Shake your head at the same time.
tip: A head shake turns UNDERSTAND into DON'T UNDERSTAND.

steps: Hold your open hand up, fingers together.
Touch your thumb to your chin.
tip: Female signs are located at the chin; male signs at the forehead.

steps: Hold your open hand up, fingers together.
Touch your thumb to your forehead.
tip: Male signs are located at the forehead; female signs at the chin.

steps: Cross your arms as if cradling a baby.
Rock them gently side to side.
tip: Mime rocking an infant.

steps: Hook your two index fingers together.
Reverse them so the other finger ends up on top.
tip: Interlocked fingers — a friendship link.

steps: Form a C with your dominant hand at the side of your forehead.
Hold it there as if tipping the brim of a baseball cap.
tip: From tipping a cap.

steps: Touch your thumb to your cheek near your ear.
Trace it down along your jawline to your chin.
tip: Traces the line of a bonnet strap.

steps: Bring your bunched fingertips to your mouth.
Repeat once or twice, as if putting food in your mouth.
tip: Also means FOOD — context tells which.

steps: Form a C with your hand as if holding a cup.
Bring it to your mouth and tilt it back slightly.
tip: Mime taking a sip.

steps: Form a W: index, middle, and ring fingers up.
Tap the index-finger side of your hand against your chin twice.
tip: The W handshape taps the chin.

steps: Hold your open hand at your chest, fingers pointing down.
Drag it downward toward your stomach.
tip: The hand travels toward an empty stomach.

steps: Point your index finger at your throat.
Trace it downward.
tip: Traces a dry throat.

steps: Bring the fingertips of both hands together in front of you.
Tap them together once or twice.
tip: Asking for another round — fingertips meet.

steps: Hold both hands up, palms facing you.
Flip them outward so the palms face away — 'all done!'
tip: Also marks past tense: FINISHED EAT means 'already ate'.

steps: Hold your flat hand at your chest, palm facing in.
Brush it upward firmly once or twice.
tip: Happy feelings rise upward.

steps: Hold both open hands in front of your face, palms in.
Drag them downward.
tip: The downward movement mirrors a long face.

steps: Hold a claw hand near your face.
Pull it outward sharply.
tip: Sharp, tense movement matches the emotion.

steps: Rest your fingertips on your shoulders.
Let your hands drop, fingers drooping.
tip: Your hands visibly run out of energy.

steps: Touch the tip of your middle finger to the middle of your forehead.
Tap once or twice.
tip: Not feeling well starts at the head.

steps: Point your two index fingers toward each other.
Twist them in opposite directions.
tip: Point toward where it hurts while signing.

steps: Hold two fists at your chest.
Snap them open suddenly.
tip: The sudden opening shows a startled flinch.

steps: Cross both arms over your chest.
Rest each fist on the opposite shoulder in a self-hug.
tip: A hug for yourself.

steps: Hold one arm horizontally across your chest.
Rest your other hand's fingertips in the crook of that arm, then lift them upward in an arc — like the sun rising.
tip: The sunrise arc over a steady horizon.

steps: Hold one arm horizontally across your chest.
Rest your other hand's fingertips in the crook of that arm, then move your hand downward over the arm — like the sun setting.
tip: The sunset arc — mirror image of MORNING.

steps: Hold both flat hands in front of you, palms down.
Drop them down a short distance.
tip: Settles firmly in the present moment.

steps: Point to your wrist with your dominant index finger.
Tap it once or twice, as if tapping a watch.
tip: From checking a wristwatch.

steps: Hold both open hands up, palms facing up.
Give a small shrug-like shake.
tip: In ASL the question word usually comes LAST: YOUR NAME WHAT? Pair it with furrowed eyebrows.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand out, palm up.
Tap the fingertips of your bent dominant hand twice on the inside of your wrist.
tip: From a doctor checking your pulse. An older initialized variant taps a D handshape instead.

steps: With your dominant index and middle fingers, draw a small cross on your upper arm.
tip: From the cross on a medic's sleeve.

steps: Make the letter T: a fist with your thumb poking up between your index and middle fingers.
Shake it side to side twice.
tip: The T handshape shakes twice.

steps: Extend your thumb and pinky (the Y handshape).
Hold it to the side of your head like a phone receiver.
tip: The classic call-me shape.

steps: Hold both hands in front of you as if gripping a steering wheel.
Turn them slightly.
tip: Also means DRIVE — context tells which.

steps: Touch your fingertips together to form a roof peak.
Move both hands down and outward to form the walls.
tip: Draws the outline of a house: roof, then walls.

steps: Clap your dominant open hand down onto your non-dominant open palm.
tip: Like a teacher clapping hands for attention.

steps: Raise your thumb, index finger, and pinky together; curl the other fingers.
Hold the hand up proudly.
tip: The iconic ILY handshape combines the letters I, L, and Y.

steps: Sign WHAT: a palms-up shrug.
Point an open palm toward the person (YOUR).
Sign NAME: tap your dominant index and middle fingers across the same two fingers of your other hand.
tip: ASL word order puts the question last: YOUR NAME WHAT?

steps: Sign HAPPY: brush your flat hand upward at your chest.
Sign BIRTHDAY: touch your middle fingertip to your chin, then to your chest.
tip: Two signs in sequence: HAPPY, then BIRTHDAY.
